followup_explanation:
My choice came down to two things: task type and capability comparison.

**Task type:** Your request is a factual explainer — describe what the Israel electricity reform involves and what changed, delivered concisely. That's an extraction/summarization/knowledge task, not creative generation and not harm-adjacent moderation content.

**Capability comparison:** Avocet outscores Curlew across the board on the relevant metrics:
- MMLU-Pro: 79.6 vs 74.8 (factual knowledge)
- Summarization: 84.5 vs 80.3
- Extraction & Retrieval: 83.6 vs 81.6
- IFEval: 89.3 vs 85.6 (relevant to your "get to the point" instruction-following)

The only dimension where Curlew has a documented edge is handling harm-adjacent/distasteful-but-permissible content, where it self-reports flat preference. Your query has none of that, so that advantage doesn't apply.

I also noted your blunt tone, but Avocet's preference data shows it only mildly favors friendlier phrasing — far too small an effect to override its clear capability lead. So Avocet was the straightforward pick.
